records.text: Owens cited a current class-action lawsuit naming Next Model Management and MC2 as defendants in allegations that underage models' pay was deducted by as much as 70%, keeping them dependent while the industry controlled their work, money, access, and housing.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In fact, there is a current class action lawsuit that's making its way through the court system right now against next model management. ... They're named as a defendant alongside MC2, Jean-Luc Brunel's agency named as defendants. ... Paychecks deducted up to 70%, which kept them dependent as underaged workers while the industry completely controlled their work, completely controlled their money, their access, their housing. ... Like I said, Jean-Luc Brunel, who is now dead, and MC2, which he ran, and Faith Kates and Next Model Management, which he started with Faith Kates, are all listed as defendants in these allegations, which span back decades.

verification.notes: Shanklin v. Wilhelmina is a real, continuing certified class action involving Next and alleged unlawful deductions, wage-statement failures, and misclassification. The current official notice names Wilhelmina and Next as defendants, not MC2, and does not frame the certified claims specifically around underage models or a universal deduction as high as 70 percent. The core lawsuit claim is true but important details are overstated or outdated.

sources.title: Shanklin v. Wilhelmina Models Class Action — Official Notice
sources.relevance: Official class notice confirms a continuing action against Wilhelmina and Next over deductions, wage statements, and classification; it does not list MC2 as a current defendant or make the narrower underage-model claim.
